title: Maximum emf calculation
description: Essential: The student must correctly calculate the maximum induced emf using E_m = nBSω, obtaining 314 V.

title: Instantaneous emf expression
description: Essential: The student must provide the correct instantaneous emf as a function of time, e = 314 sin(100πt) V.

title: Average emf calculation
description: Essential: The student must correctly calculate the average emf from t=0 to T/4, obtaining 200 V.

title: Application of Faraday's law
description: Important: The student must apply Faraday's law for a rotating coil, recognizing the sinusoidal dependence on ωt.

title: Flux change reasoning
description: Important: For the average emf, the student must correctly compute the change in magnetic flux ΔΦ from the neutral plane to the perpendicular position.

title: Area calculation
description: Optional: The student calculates the coil area S = l_AB * l_BC = 0.1 m².

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: The student's final answers include correct units (Volts) and the argument of the sine function is dimensionless.

title: Sign or phase error
description: Pitfall: The student uses cosine instead of sine for the instantaneous emf, given the timing starts when the coil passes through the neutral plane.

title: Average emf formula misuse
description: Pitfall: The student incorrectly uses (E_m/√2) or (2/π)E_m in the wrong context for the average over a quarter period.
